Priority Principle: Tight cast

Why Not Others: (a) Walking on the cast adds to the pressure; (b) A hot pack does not free the tight cast; (d) Waiting lets the skin and nerve suffer.

PGI Exam Trap: The sign is noted for the next ward round.

5-Second Recall: Tell the doctor and loosen the cast.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cold pale toes mean free the cast.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward is asked which statement about the sunken soft spot of a baby is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It has no meaning for the nurse at all
option_2: It shows the baby has been well fed
option_3: It is a sign of too much water in the baby
option_4: It is a sign of NOT enough fluid in the baby
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It is a sign of NOT enough fluid in the baby

Clinical Rationale: A sunken soft spot in a baby is a sign that the baby does NOT have enough fluid in the body.

Key Clue: what a sunken soft spot means

Priority Principle: Sunken fontanelle

Why Not Others: (a) It does have a clear meaning; (b) A well fed baby does not have a sunken spot; (c) It points to too little, not too much, fluid.

PGI Exam Trap: A sunken soft spot shows the baby is well fed.

5-Second Recall: A sunken soft spot means not enough fluid.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sunken spot means dried out.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in labour notes a sudden gush of fluid and a cord seen at the vulva. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Kneel her with the head down and call for help
option_2: Push the cord gently back inside
option_3: Ask her to walk to the labour room
option_4: Note it and wait for the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Kneel her with the head down and call for help

Clinical Rationale: A cord seen at the vulva after a gush of fluid can be squeezed and cut off the baby's oxygen, so she is knelt head down and help called.

Key Clue: a gush of fluid with the cord at the vulva

Priority Principle: Cord prolapse

Why Not Others: (b) Pushing the cord back can kink it; (c) Walking squeezes the cord further; (d) Waiting cuts the baby's oxygen.

PGI Exam Trap: The cord is pushed gently back inside.

5-Second Recall: Kneel her with the head down and call for help.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cord down, head down, call help.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes a water tablet each day notes that he is dizzy on standing and his mouth is dry. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give another water tablet at once
option_2: Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor
option_3: Hold back all of his fluids
option_4: Ask him to stand up quickly
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Dizziness on standing with a dry mouth on a water tablet points to too little fluid, so the blood pressure is checked and the doctor told.

Key Clue: dizziness on standing while on a water tablet

Priority Principle: Fluid loss from a diuretic

Why Not Others: (a) Another water tablet worsens the loss; (c) Holding back fluids makes it worse; (d) Standing up quickly may cause a fall.

PGI Exam Trap: Another water tablet is given at once.

5-Second Recall: Check his blood pressure and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dizzy and dry means check the pressure.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about giving a pain killer into the muscle is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is given into the upper outer part of the buttock
option_2: It is given into the middle of the buttock
option_3: It is given after the drug is wiped off
option_4: It is given without checking the order
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It is given into the upper outer part of the buttock

Clinical Rationale: A pain killer given into the muscle goes into the upper outer part of the buttock, which is away from the large nerve.

Key Clue: the safe site for a muscle injection

Priority Principle: Intramuscular injection

Why Not Others: (b) The middle of the buttock holds a large nerve; (c) The drug is never wiped off; (d) The order is checked before the drug.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is given into the middle of the buttock.

5-Second Recall: It is given into the upper outer part of the buttock.

PNC Exam Pearl: Upper outer, away from the nerve.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes a drug for schizophrenia notes that his neck is stiff and his eyes roll up. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop all his drugs and send him home
option_2: Tell the doctor and give the ordered drug for it
option_3: Ignore it as a common finding
option_4: Give a double dose of the same drug
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Tell the doctor and give the ordered drug for it

Clinical Rationale: A stiff neck with rolling eyes points to a drug side effect called dystonia, so the doctor is told and the ordered drug for it is given.

Key Clue: a stiff neck with rolling eyes on a drug

Priority Principle: Drug induced dystonia

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping all drugs without advice is unsafe; (c) Ignoring it lets the spasm worsen; (d) A double dose of the same drug worsens it.

PGI Exam Trap: The finding is ignored as a common one.

5-Second Recall: Tell the doctor and give the ordered drug for it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stiff neck on a drug means tell the doctor.

question: A nurse caring for an elderly woman on the ward who has been in bed for a week notes a reddened area over her heel that does NOT fade when pressed. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Rest her weight on that heel for a while
option_2: Rub the red area hard with some cream
option_3: Keep her off that heel and tell the doctor
option_4: Note it for the next ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Keep her off that heel and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A reddened area that does NOT fade points to an early pressure sore, so the heel is kept off the bed and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: a red heel that does NOT fade on an elderly woman

Priority Principle: Early pressure sore

Why Not Others: (a) Resting on the heel presses the sore; (b) Rubbing hard harms the skin further; (d) Waiting lets the sore deepen.

PGI Exam Trap: The reddened area is rubbed hard with cream.

5-Second Recall: Keep her off that heel and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Red that will not fade means off the heel.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to insert a suppository into a 50-year-old man. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Insert it while he is standing up
option_2: Insert it FIRST and then explain the step
option_3: Lie him on his left side, insert it, then explain
option_4: Explain the step, lie him on his left side, then insert it
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Explain the step, lie him on his left side, then insert it

Clinical Rationale: The nurse explains the step, lies the man on his left side, and then inserts the suppository, so it is done with care and stays in place.

Key Clue: the steps for inserting a suppository

Priority Principle: Suppository order

Why Not Others: (a) He is not standing when it is inserted; (b) The step is explained before it is done; (c) The explanation comes first of all.

PGI Exam Trap: It is inserted while he is standing up.

5-Second Recall: Explain the step, lie him on his left side, then insert it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Explain, lie left, then insert.

question: A community nurse visiting a family finds that many children in the school have dental decay. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Teach brushing and arrange a fluoride rinse
option_2: Tell the children to eat more sweets
option_3: Wait for the milk teeth to fall out
option_4: Give the children no advice at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Teach brushing and arrange a fluoride rinse

Clinical Rationale: Teaching the children to brush well and arranging a fluoride rinse lowers dental decay among the school children.

Key Clue: many children with dental decay at school

Priority Principle: Dental decay

Why Not Others: (b) More sweets raise the decay; (c) Waiting lets the decay spread to new teeth; (d) No advice leaves the decay.

PGI Exam Trap: The children are told to eat more sweets.

5-Second Recall: Teach brushing and arrange a fluoride rinse.

PNC Exam Pearl: Brush and rinse.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward reads a lab report that says his wound swab is growing a germ that resists many antibiotics. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give the same antibiotic once again
option_2: Tell the doctor and check the wound care
option_3: Set the report aside as it means nothing
option_4: Stop cleaning the hands before care
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Tell the doctor and check the wound care

Clinical Rationale: A germ that resists many antibiotics needs the right drug, so the doctor is told and the wound care is checked to stop the spread.

Key Clue: a swab growing a germ that resists many drugs

Priority Principle: Resistant germ

Why Not Others: (a) The same drug may not work on this germ; (c) The report is important, not ignored; (d) Hand cleaning is never stopped.

PGI Exam Trap: The report is set aside as it means nothing.

5-Second Recall: Tell the doctor and check the wound care.

PNC Exam Pearl: Resistant germ, tell the doctor.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about giving a drug under the tongue is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It is given together with a large meal
option_2: It is swallowed at once with water
option_3: It is taken in quickly and he must NOT swallow it
option_4: It is put on the skin instead
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is taken in quickly and he must NOT swallow it

Clinical Rationale: A drug given under the tongue is taken in quickly into the blood and the man must NOT swallow it, so the dose works fast.

Key Clue: giving a drug under the tongue

Priority Principle: Sublingual drug

Why Not Others: (a) A large meal is not needed for this route; (b) Swallowing it slows the action; (d) It goes under the tongue, not on the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: It is swallowed at once with water.

5-Second Recall: It is taken in quickly and he must not swallow it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Under the tongue, do not swallow.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the normal pulse rate of an adult at rest is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It changes with no pattern at all
option_2: It lies between 20 and 40 beats a minute
option_3: It lies between 130 and 150 beats a minute
option_4: It lies between 60 and 100 beats a minute
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It lies between 60 and 100 beats a minute

Clinical Rationale: The normal pulse rate of an adult at rest lies between 60 and 100 beats a minute.

Key Clue: the normal pulse rate of an adult

Priority Principle: Normal pulse

Why Not Others: (a) The resting rate has a set range; (b) 20 to 40 beats a minute is far too slow; (c) 130 to 150 beats a minute is far too fast.

PGI Exam Trap: The normal pulse lies between 20 and 40 beats a minute.

5-Second Recall: The normal pulse lies between 60 and 100 a minute.

PNC Exam Pearl: Six to ten tens a minute.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visiting a family is shown a growth chart for the village in which the weight line has fallen over 3 months. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Look for feeding problems and screen the children
option_2: Wait for the weight line to rise on its own
option_3: Tell the families that all is well
option_4: Give the families no advice about feeding
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look for feeding problems and screen the children

Clinical Rationale: A weight line that has fallen over 3 months points to poor feeding in the village, so the nurse looks for the cause and screens the children.

Key Clue: a growth chart with a weight line fallen over 3 months

Priority Principle: Poor growth in a village

Why Not Others: (b) Waiting lets the poor growth go on; (c) Telling the families that all is well is wrong; (d) Feeding advice is needed now.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse waits for the weight line to rise on its own.

5-Second Recall: Look for feeding problems and screen the children.

PNC Exam Pearl: Falling line means find the cause.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes lithium is asked which sign is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A fine tremor with a steady mood
option_2: A coarse tremor with vomiting and blurred vision
option_3: A good appetite at the meal times
option_4: A steady pulse of 78 bpm
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A coarse tremor with vomiting and blurred vision

Clinical Rationale: A coarse tremor with vomiting and blurred vision on lithium points to too much drug in the blood, so it is reported at once.

Key Clue: a coarse tremor with vomiting on lithium

Priority Principle: Lithium toxicity

Why Not Others: (a) A fine tremor with a steady mood is expected; (c) A good appetite is not a sign of toxicity; (d) A steady pulse of 78 bpm is normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady pulse of 78 bpm is reported as toxicity.

5-Second Recall: A coarse tremor with vomiting is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Coarse tremor means too much lithium.

Reference Table: Therapeutic drug levels & monitoring - Digoxin: 0.5-2.0 ng/mL (toxic > 2.0); Lithium: 0.6-1.2 mEq/L (toxic > 1.5); Phenytoin: 10-20 mcg/mL; INR (warfarin): Therapeutic 2-3; aPTT (heparin): 1.5-2.5 x control.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a person with a new stoma is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: He is given no teaching about the stoma
option_2: He is told that the stoma will close by itself
option_3: He is shown how to care for it before he goes home
option_4: He is asked to keep away from the stoma
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) He is shown how to care for it before he goes home

Clinical Rationale: A man with a new stoma is shown how to care for it before he goes home, so that he can manage it with confidence.

Key Clue: the teaching for a person with a new stoma

Priority Principle: Stoma teaching

Why Not Others: (a) Teaching is needed before he goes home; (b) A stoma does not close by itself; (d) He is not kept away from his own stoma.

PGI Exam Trap: He is told that the stoma will close by itself.

5-Second Recall: He is shown how to care for it before he goes home.

PNC Exam Pearl: Teach the stoma before home.

question: A nurse caring for a family in the community is asked which statement about a safe drinking water supply is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Water needs no care at all
option_2: Water is taken straight from the open well
option_3: Water is kept in the same dirty pot
option_4: Water is boiled or filtered before it is drunk
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Water is boiled or filtered before it is drunk

Clinical Rationale: Water is boiled or filtered before it is drunk, so that the germs that cause diarrhoea are killed.

Key Clue: how to keep drinking water safe

Priority Principle: Safe water

Why Not Others: (a) Water does need care; (b) Open well water carries germs; (c) A dirty pot adds more germs.

PGI Exam Trap: Water is taken straight from the open well.

5-Second Recall: Water is boiled or filtered before it is drunk.

PNC Exam Pearl: Boil it or filter it.
